lines.idea: Here's an idea. Want to try it?
lines.best_q: Which part was the best? Show me!
lines.best_reply: Mine too! I loved that part.
lines.sticker: A new sticker for your sticker book!
lines.sticker_gold: A shiny gold sticker, because you did the challenge!
lines.sticker_again: You made it again! Look, your sticker is still here.
lines.book: This is your book of things you made.
lines.bye: Bye bye! Go and show everyone!
lines.checkin_seeds: How are your seeds? Show me!
lines.checkin_hanky: Did you touch the two hankies? Which one is dry?

stuck_generic.say: Ask Amma or Appa to help you. Two hands are better than one!
Let's watch it again, slowly. Then you try.
Try again, slowly. Every try teaches your hands something new!

activities.title: Draw your family

hook.say: I drew my whole sparrow family, but I have never seen yours! Will you draw everyone at home?

activities.fun: He becomes the family's illustrator: big people, small people, and who is who.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Now draw everyone who lives in your home. Big people and small people!

stuck.say: Start with a big round head. Then a body, two arms and two legs.
Draw yourself first. Then draw the next person, right next to you.

steps.say: Do you want to add Ajji, Thatha, or someone else you love?
Point to each one. Who is this? And who is this?

twist.say: Now give everyone at home a silly hat. Even Ajji!

challenge.say: Can you give everyone five fingers on each hand? Count them!

activities.show: Show your drawing to Amma or Appa!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me who is in your family picture.
activities.why: Drawing a whole person is a UKG fine-motor goal, and naming family builds talk and belonging (CG-4, CG-12).

activities.title: My favourite animal

hook.say: The animals at Bannerghatta want a picture! Which animal do you love most? Draw it big!

activities.fun: Big, bold drawing plus talking about tails, ears, stripes and homes.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Close your eyes. Which animal do you love the most?
Draw your animal big, big, big! Does it have a tail? Ears? Stripes?

stuck.say: Start with a big round body. Then add a head, legs and a tail.
Look at a toy or a book picture of your animal. What shape is it?

steps.say: Where does your animal live? In a forest, in the sea, or in a house?

twist.say: What if your animal had wings? Draw some on it!

challenge.say: Can you draw the animal's baby next to it? Make it small!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa, and make your animal's sound!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me about your animal. What sound does it make?
activities.why: Links an animal to its habitat and lets him describe features in full sentences (CG-6, CG-9).

activities.title: What I saw in the video

hook.say: I fell asleep in my nest and missed the video! Can you draw me one thing you saw?
hook.text: Draw what you saw for me

mission.text: Draw one thing from the video

activities.fun: Turning a video into a drawing and a story is how watching becomes learning.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Think about the video. What is one thing you saw?

stuck.say: What was the funniest part? Or the most surprising? Draw that one.
Who was in the video? Start by drawing them.

steps.say: Draw that one thing. Take your time.
Now tell the story of your picture. What is happening?

twist.say: Now draw the same thing again, but at night time!

challenge.say: Fold your paper into three boxes. Draw the start, the middle, and the end!

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa about your picture!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you drew from the video.
activities.why: Recalling and retelling one idea from a video is how watching turns into learning (CG-9, CG-13).

activities.title: Feelings faces

hook.say: I am a little bird, so I can't make faces! Can you draw happy, sad and surprised faces for me?

activities.fun: He gets to be the face-maker, and names feelings out loud.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Draw a happy face. Is the mouth going up?

stuck.say: Draw a big circle. Two dots for eyes. Then a mouth that curves up, like a smile.

steps.say: Now draw a sad face. Where do the tears go?

stuck.say: For sad, the mouth curves down. Add one tear under an eye.

steps.say: Now a surprised face! Big round eyes, big round mouth.
Tell Amma or Appa: when do you feel happy? When do you feel sad?

twist.say: Can you draw a silly face? Or a sleepy face?

challenge.say: Can you draw a cross face? The eyebrows go down, like this!

activities.show: Show your faces to Amma or Appa. Can they guess each one?
activities.done: Wow! Which face did you like drawing most?
activities.why: Naming and drawing feelings builds emotional vocabulary, the base of self-calming (CG-4).

activities.title: Hand-shape bird

hook.say: I want a new friend to fly with! Can your hand turn into a bird? Let's find out!

mission.text: Turn your hand into a bird

activities.fun: Tracing his own hand is magic: it becomes a peacock.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Put your hand flat on the paper. Draw slowly around each finger.

stuck.say: Spread your fingers and keep your hand very still. Draw slowly, like an ant walking.
Ask someone to hold the paper still for you.

steps.say: Can your hand become a peacock or a hen? Add an eye and legs.

stuck.say: Your thumb is the bird's head. Add an eye and a beak. Fingers are feathers!

steps.say: Now colour your bird. Which colours will you use?

twist.say: Now draw around your foot. What can it become?

challenge.say: Draw around your hand three times. Make a whole bird family!

activities.show: Show your hand-bird to Amma or Appa!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me about your hand-bird.
activities.why: Tracing strengthens pencil control, and turning a shape into something new is imagination at work (CG-12).

activities.title: The night sky

hook.say: It's bedtime in my nest, but I can't sleep without stars. Can you draw me a night sky?

activities.fun: A calm drawing with counting built in: every star is a number.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Draw the moon. Is it round, or a thin smile?

stuck.say: A thin moon looks like a banana. Draw a curve, then another curve inside.

steps.say: Now add stars. Count them as you draw. One, two, three...

stuck.say: An easy star: draw a plus, then a cross on top. Like this!

steps.say: Who is awake at night? An owl? Draw a night-time friend.

twist.say: Draw a rocket flying up to the moon. Whoosh!

challenge.say: Can you draw exactly ten stars? Count each one as you draw!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa, and count your stars together!
activities.done: Wow! How many stars did you draw?
activities.why: Counting while drawing practises one-to-one counting, and talks about day and night (CG-7, CG-8).

activities.title: My breakfast plate

hook.say: I only peck grains for breakfast! What was on your plate today? Idli? Dosa? Draw it for me!

activities.fun: Talking about real home food: idli circles, dosa triangles, chutney colours.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: What did you have for breakfast today? Idli? Dosa? Upma?
Draw a big round plate.

stuck.say: Put a steel plate on the paper and draw around it. A perfect circle!

steps.say: Now draw your breakfast on the plate. What colours does it have?

stuck.say: Idli is a white circle. Dosa is a big triangle, or a roll!

twist.say: Give your breakfast a funny face!

challenge.say: Draw a second plate. What do you want for dinner tonight?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your plate and tell your favourite part!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what is on your plate.
activities.why: Talking about real food builds vocabulary about healthy habits and circles as a shape (CG-1, CG-8).

activities.title: Kolam dots

hook.say: Every morning, Ajji draws a kolam at the door. Can you draw one for my nest?
hook.text: Draw a kolam for my nest

activities.fun: A family tradition that is secretly maths: rows, counting, symmetry.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Make three rows of dots, like Amma's kolam. Three dots in each row.

stuck.say: Put one finger between each dot. Then the dots are not too close.

steps.say: Join the dots with curvy lines. Loop around them, slowly.

stuck.say: Go round each dot like a snake, slowly. Try not to touch the dots.
Easy start: join the dots in a plus shape first.

steps.say: Colour your kolam. Make both sides the same, if you like.

twist.say: Try again with four rows of dots. A bigger kolam!

challenge.say: Can you make the left side and the right side look the same, like butterfly wings?

activities.show: Show your kolam to Amma or Appa!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me about your kolam.
activities.why: Dot-grid kolam builds pattern, symmetry and counting through a family tradition (CG-8, CG-12).

activities.title: Today's weather

hook.say: I want to fly to Lalbagh today. Is it sunny or rainy? Can you check the sky for me?

activities.fun: He is the family weather reporter, and dresses himself for it on paper.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Look out of the window. What is the sky doing?
Is it sunny, cloudy, or rainy today? Is the wind moving the trees?

stuck.say: Look at the trees. Are the leaves moving? Then it's windy!
Is the sky grey and dark? Rain might come soon!

steps.say: Draw the sky as it is today.
Now draw yourself, wearing the right clothes for this weather.

twist.say: What if a rainbow came out? Draw one in your sky!

challenge.say: Look again in the evening. Is the sky the same, or different? Draw it!

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa what the weather is today!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what the weather is today.
activities.why: Observing and recording the weather is early science: noticing and describing (CG-6, CG-7).

activities.title: Big and small

hook.say: An ant told me he is the biggest animal in the world! Is that true? Let's draw and see!

activities.fun: Proving a silly ant wrong teaches big, small and comparing.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Draw something very big. A bus? An elephant? A tree?

stuck.say: Big means it fills almost the whole paper, from top to bottom!

steps.say: Now, next to it, draw something tiny. An ant? A tiny flower?

stuck.say: Tiny means as small as your fingernail.

steps.say: Point and say: this one is big, this one is small.

twist.text: A house for the tiny one
twist.say: Now draw a tiny house for your tiny thing.

challenge.say: Draw something in the middle: not big, not tiny. Then point: big, middle, small!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your big and small picture!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what is big and what is small.
activities.why: Comparing sizes and using words like bigger and smaller is a UKG measurement goal (CG-8).

activities.title: When I grow up

hook.say: When I grow up, I want to be a pilot! What do you want to be? Draw it for me!

activities.fun: Dreaming out loud: jobs, tools and who helps our city.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: When you grow big, what do you want to be? A doctor? A farmer? A cricketer?

stuck.say: Think of people you see. The bus driver? The doctor? The vegetable seller?

steps.say: Draw yourself as a grown-up, doing that job.

stuck.say: Draw yourself first. Then add a work hat or a uniform.

steps.say: What tools will you use? Draw them next to you.

twist.text: How will you go to work?
twist.say: How will you go to work? Draw your bus, car, or cycle.

challenge.say: Where will you work? A hospital, a farm, a cricket ground? Draw it all around you!

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa about your job!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you will be.
activities.why: Imagining a future self and naming helpers' tools builds confidence and community awareness (CG-4, CG-5).

activities.title: My cricket game

hook.say: Imagine you hit a huge six at Chinnaswamy stadium! Can you draw it for me?

activities.fun: Cricket plus drawing motion: where did the ball fly, high or low?
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Draw a bat and a ball. Is the ball red or white?
Now draw yourself hitting the ball. Swing!

stuck.say: Draw a stick person first: a circle and lines. Then put the bat in the hands.

steps.say: Draw a dotted line where the ball flew. High or low? Near or far?

twist.say: Draw people cheering for you. Hooray!

challenge.say: Draw the crowd and the big stadium lights all around you!

activities.show: Show Appa, then play a little catch together!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me about your cricket picture.
activities.why: Drawing a movement he knows helps him plan the action, and leads into real ball play (CG-3, CG-12).

activities.title: Map of my room

hook.say: I fly up high and look down. Everything looks so small! Can you draw your room like a bird?
hook.text: Draw your room like a bird

mission.text: Draw a map of your room

activities.fun: His first map: seeing his own room from above is a big thinking leap.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and crayons.

steps.say: Stand in your room. What is in it? A bed? A cupboard? A door?

steps.text: Draw it like a bird sees
steps.say: Pretend you are a bird, looking down from the ceiling. Draw your bed and your door.

stuck.say: From the top, a bed is just a long box. Draw a rectangle!
Start with the door. Then draw what is next to it.

steps.say: Put a star where your toys live.
Show your map. Walk your finger from the door to your bed.

twist.say: Draw a secret treasure on your map. Can Appa find it?

challenge.say: Can you draw a map of your whole home? The hall, Amma's room and your room!

activities.show: Give Amma or Appa a tour of your map!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me where your toys live on your map.
activities.why: Drawing from above is early map thinking: position words like near, next to and behind (CG-7, CG-8).

activities.title: Rangoli with powder

hook.say: It's festival time! Every home needs a rangoli at the door. Shall we make one together?

activities.fun: Real rangoli powder, a real festival skill, side by side with Amma.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need rangoli powder and a floor spot.

steps.say: Ask Amma or Appa for a little rangoli powder. Do it together, on the floor.
With a tiny pinch, make a few dots on the floor.
Take a pinch. Let it fall slowly from your fingers, making a line.

stuck.say: Hold the powder between your thumb and finger. Rub them slowly, and it falls.
Move your hand very slowly. Slow hand, nice line.

steps.say: Fill the shapes with colours. Keep your hands away from your eyes.

twist.say: Make a flower right in the middle of your rangoli.

challenge.say: Can you join dots to make a star shape? Ask Amma to show you one.

activities.show: Show your rangoli to everyone at home!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me which colours you used.
activities.why: The pinch-and-pour grip builds the same finger strength as holding a pencil, inside a festival tradition (CG-2, CG-12).

activities.title: Tall block tower

hook.say: A naughty wind knocked down my block tower! Can you build a new one, even taller?

activities.fun: Stacking, guessing and counting, and knocking it down is allowed.
activities.gather_say: You need blocks and a box.

steps.say: Put one block on top of another. Slowly, slowly.

stuck.say: Put the biggest blocks at the bottom. Small ones go on top.
Put each block down slowly, right in the middle.

steps.say: Guess! How many blocks before it falls?
Count your blocks. Did it fall? Build again, even taller!

twist.say: Can your tower hold a tiny toy on top?

challenge.say: Can you build it taller than your knee? Stand next to it and check!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your tower before it falls!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me how tall your tower got.
activities.why: Stacking trains balance, hand control and counting, and rebuilding after a fall practises persistence (CG-8, CG-13).

activities.title: Shapes with pencils

hook.say: I tried to make a triangle with sticks for my nest, but it fell apart! Can you show me how?

activities.fun: Shapes he can hold: count the sides, then build a house.
activities.gather_say: You need pencils and crayons.

steps.say: Lay three pencils on the floor. Make their ends touch. A triangle!

stuck.say: Make each pencil end touch the next pencil's end. No gaps!
Pencils that are the same size make a neat triangle.

steps.say: Now try four pencils. Can you make a square?
How many pencils for a house? A square with a triangle roof!

stuck.say: Make the square first. Then lean two pencils on top for a roof.

twist.say: Can you make a fish with pencils? Try a triangle tail!

challenge.say: Can you make a diamond? It's a square standing on its corner!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your shapes and count the sides!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me which shapes you built.
activities.why: Building shapes from sides makes 2D shapes concrete: three sides, four sides (CG-8).

activities.title: Chappal train

hook.say: Toot toot! The chappal train is going to Mysuru, but the carriages are lost. Can you find them?

activities.fun: Ordering by size with the whole family's chappals, plus counting carriages.
activities.gather_say: You need chappals and shoes.

steps.say: Go to the door. Bring all the chappals and shoes to one place.
Line them up, one behind the other, like a train.
Can you put the biggest chappal first, and the smallest one last?

stuck.say: Put two chappals side by side. Which one is longer? That one goes first.
Whose chappal is the biggest? Appa's? Start the train with that one!

steps.say: Count your train carriages. Then wash your hands!

twist.say: Make your chappal train go around a corner. Choo choo!

challenge.say: Close your eyes. Ask Amma to take one chappal away. Which carriage is missing?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your chappal train!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me about your chappal train.
activities.why: Putting things in order by size (seriation) and counting are core UKG number skills (CG-8).

activities.title: Paper fan

hook.say: Phew! It's so hot in my nest today. Can you make me a paper fan?

activities.fun: Folding back and forth, then a real cool breeze he made himself.
activities.gather_say: You need one paper.

steps.say: Fold a small strip. Turn the paper over. Fold again. A zig-zag!

stuck.say: Fold a strip. Flip the paper over. Fold again. Fold, flip, fold, flip!
Make each strip as thin as your finger.

steps.say: Keep folding to the end. Squeeze one end tight.
Open it out and fan Amma gently. Ahh, cool wind!

twist.say: Colour stripes first, then fold. A rainbow fan!

challenge.say: Make three fans and put them side by side. A peacock tail!

activities.show: Give Amma or Appa a cool breeze with your fan!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me how your fan feels.
activities.why: Repeated folding builds finger strength and a sense of pattern, and he feels air moving (CG-2, CG-7).

activities.title: Book domino line

hook.say: I saw dominoes fall: click, click, click! Can books fall like that too?

activities.fun: A chain reaction he sets up and sets off: guess, push, watch.
activities.gather_say: You need books, big and small.

steps.say: Stand the books up in a long line, with a little gap between each.

stuck.say: Leave a gap of two fingers between books. Not too far!
Open each book a little, so it stands up by itself.

steps.say: Guess! If you push the first book, what will happen?
Push the first book gently. Watch!
Try a longer line, or a curvy one. Does it still work?

twist.say: Mix blocks into your book line. Do they still fall?

challenge.say: Can you make the line curve like a snake, and still fall?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your domino line falling!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what happened to your books.
activities.why: Setting up a chain and predicting the result is cause-and-effect thinking (CG-7).

activities.title: Book bridge

hook.say: My toy car wants to cross the river, but there is no bridge! Can you build one?

activities.fun: Engineering at floor level: will it hold the car? A heavier toy?
activities.gather_say: You need books, newspaper and a toy car.

steps.say: Make two piles of books, a little bit apart.
Lay a folded newspaper across the top, from one pile to the other.

stuck.say: Is the paper falling in? Move the piles closer together.
Fold the newspaper again to make it thicker and stronger.

steps.say: Drive a small toy car across your bridge. Does it hold?
What if you put a heavier toy on it? Guess, then try!

twist.say: Now make a tiny bridge for an ant, with two small books.

challenge.say: Move the piles further apart. Can your bridge still hold the car?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your bridge and what it can hold!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what your bridge could hold.
activities.why: Testing what a bridge can hold is early engineering: strong, weak, heavy, light (CG-7, CG-8).

activities.title: Steel tumbler tower

hook.say: Oh no! My steel tumbler tower fell down. Can you build a taller one?

activities.fun: Shiny steel, a satisfying clink, and real balance-and-floors building.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need steel tumblers and steel plates.

steps.say: Turn three tumblers upside down on the floor.
Put a plate on top of them, like a floor.
Add more tumblers and another plate. Build it higher!

stuck.say: Put the tumblers near the edges of the plate, not in the middle.
Plates that are the same size make a steady floor.

steps.say: How many floors can you make before it wobbles?

twist.say: Can teddy sit inside your tower, like a house?

challenge.say: Can your tower be taller than your knee? Build it slowly!

activities.show: Show Amma your tower, then help put everything back!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me how many floors you built.
activities.why: Balancing and layering teaches stability, and putting things back is seva (CG-5, CG-7).

activities.title: Toy car track

hook.say: My toy car wants to visit Thatha, but it doesn't know the way! Can you build a track?

mission.text: Build a track for the car

activities.fun: Tearing paper (allowed!) and building a little town to drive through.
activities.gather_say: You need old newspaper, a toy car and blocks.

steps.say: Tear old newspaper into long strips. Rrrip!

stuck.say: Hold the top with both hands. Pull one hand down, slowly. Rrrip!

steps.text: Lay a track on the floor
steps.say: Lay the strips on the floor to make a long track. Make it turn!

stuck.say: To turn, start a new strip pointing a new way.

steps.say: Put blocks next to the track for houses and shops.
Drive your car along the track, all the way home.

twist.say: Add a book bridge to your track. Up and over!

challenge.say: Make a stop sign and a go sign from paper. Stop, go, stop!

activities.show: Give Amma or Appa a ride along your track!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me where your track goes.
activities.why: Tearing builds hand strength; planning a route builds spatial words like left, right and along (CG-2, CG-7).

activities.title: Teddy's box house

hook.say: Teddy has no home! He's sleeping on the floor. Can you make him a house?

mission.text: Make a box house for teddy

activities.fun: A real cardboard house with a door he drew, and a story about who lives there.
activities.gather_say: You need an empty box, crayons and teddy.

steps.say: Find an empty cardboard box.
Draw a door and windows on the box.

stuck.say: A door is a tall rectangle. Windows are small squares.

steps.say: Fold a hanky to make a bed. Put your teddy inside.

stuck.say: Fold the hanky in half, then in half again. A soft little bed!

steps.say: Who lives in your house? What do they do all day?

twist.say: Draw a garden around teddy's house. Flowers? A tree?

challenge.say: Teddy is lonely. Make a second house next door for a friend!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa the house and its family!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me who lives in your box house.
activities.why: Building a home for a toy sparks pretend play and storytelling, key for language at this age (CG-9, CG-12).

activities.title: A cosy nest

hook.say: Rain came and my nest got wet! Can you make me a soft new nest?

mission.text: Make a soft nest for me

activities.fun: He builds a home for the buddy, then compares it with real bird nests.
activities.gather_say: You need old socks, a hanky and newspaper.

steps.say: Find soft things: a hanky, old socks, bits of newspaper.
Shape them into a round nest, like a little basket.

stuck.say: Make a ring with a sock first. Then fill the middle with soft things.
Press the middle down with your fist to make a hollow.

steps.say: Put a small toy inside. Is it cosy?
Birds build nests with just their beaks and feet! What did you use?

twist.say: Scrunch some paper into little eggs for your nest.

challenge.say: Can your nest hold a bigger toy? Make the walls higher!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your nest!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you used for your nest.
activities.why: Making a nest helps him wonder how animals build homes and compare that with his hands (CG-6, CG-7).

activities.title: Newspaper tent tower

hook.say: All the blocks are hiding! Can we build a tall tower from just newspaper?

activities.fun: Paper is floppy until you fold it: a real engineering surprise.
activities.gather_say: You need old newspaper.

steps.say: Fold a sheet in half and stand it up, like a little tent.

stuck.say: Open the fold a little, like a book standing up.
Too floppy? Fold the sheet in half first, then make the tent.

steps.say: Make three tents and stand them in a row.

steps.text: Put a flat paper on top
steps.say: Lay a flat newspaper on top. That's the first floor!
Add more tents and another floor. How tall can it go?

stuck.say: Put the tents right under the corners of the floor paper.

twist.say: Can your paper tower hold a small toy on top?

challenge.text: As tall as a chair seat
challenge.say: Can your paper tower be as tall as a chair seat?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your paper tower!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me how many floors your paper tower has.
activities.why: Discovering that a fold makes flat paper strong is real engineering, done with trial and error (CG-7, CG-13).

activities.title: Cushion fort

hook.say: Let's pretend we are explorers in the jungle! We need a cosy fort for the night. Will you build one?

activities.fun: Pretend play with real building, then a cosy reading den.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need cushions and pillows, a bedsheet and a book.

steps.say: Stand them up on the floor to make walls.

stuck.say: Lean two cushions against each other, like a tent. They hold each other up.
Use the sofa as one big wall. Ask Appa first!

steps.say: Ask Appa to put a bedsheet on top for a roof.
Crawl inside with a book or your teddy. So cosy!

twist.say: Make a door for your fort that opens and closes.

challenge.say: Make a secret password. Only people who say it can come in!

activities.show: Invite Amma or Appa into your fort!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what is inside your fort.
activities.why: Planning a space and working with a grown-up builds problem-solving and cooperation (CG-4, CG-7).

activities.title: Paper lantern

hook.say: Deepavali is here! Every window has a lantern, but my nest has none. Will you make me one?

activities.fun: A real festival craft with Appa, cutting with child scissors side by side.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need coloured paper and child scissors.

steps.say: Fold a paper in half, the long way. Press it flat.
With Appa, use child scissors. Cut lines from the fold, but stop before the end.

stuck.say: Stop cutting one finger before the edge. Appa can draw a stop line.
Appa holds the paper. You cut slowly, eyes on the scissors.

steps.say: Open it up. Roll it round, and Appa joins the ends.

stuck.say: Roll it gently. Appa joins the ends with tape or glue.

steps.say: Ask Appa to hang your lantern up high. Just paper, just for looking.

twist.say: Colour the paper first. A rainbow lantern!

challenge.say: Make three lanterns in different colours. Hang them in a row!

activities.show: Show everyone your lantern!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me where your lantern is hanging.
activities.why: Cutting with child scissors is a named UKG fine-motor goal; here it makes a festival decoration (CG-2, CG-12).

activities.title: Build your letter

hook.say: I want to put your name on my nest! Which letter does your name start with? Let's build it!

mission.text: Build your letter on the floor

activities.fun: His own letter, big enough to walk around, made from socks and pencils.
activities.gather_say: You need blocks, socks and pencils.

steps.say: Your name starts with a letter. Do you remember which one?

stuck.say: Look at your name on your school bag or book. The first letter is the big one!

steps.say: Make that letter on the floor with blocks, pencils, or socks.

stuck.say: Make the straight lines first. Then add the curvy parts with socks.

steps.say: Now ask Amma: which letter does her name start with? Make that one too!

twist.say: Now make your letter with only socks. Or with chappals!

challenge.say: Now build the first letter of Appa's name, and Ajji's too!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your letters!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me which letters you built.
activities.why: Building a letter with objects gives its shape a body memory, with no writing pressure (CG-10).

activities.title: Red things hunt

hook.say: My favourite colour is red, like a tomato! Can you find three red things to show me?

activities.fun: A colour hunt round the house, with counting at the end.
activities.gather_say: You need sharp eyes.

steps.say: Look all around the room with your sharp eyes.
Can you find three red things?

stuck.say: Red can be a tomato, a toy, a book, or Amma's bindi!
Look at your clothes and your toys. Anything red?

steps.say: Bring them all to one place.
Count them. One, two, three!

challenge.say: Now find three orange things. Is a carrot orange? Is a marigold?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your red treasures!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what red things you found.
activities.why: Sorting by colour is the first step of classifying, and counting the haul is one-to-one counting (CG-2, CG-8).

activities.title: Round things hunt

hook.say: I love round things: round eggs, round eyes, round me! Can you find three round things?

activities.fun: Shape-spotting in real life: a plate, a clock, a ball.
activities.gather_say: You need sharp eyes.

steps.say: Let's look for round things!
A plate is round. A clock is round. What else is round?
Find three round things. Bring the small ones, point to the big ones.

stuck.say: Run your finger around the edge. No corners? Then it's round!

steps.say: Tell where you found each one.

challenge.say: Find three square things. Square things have four corners!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your round things!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what round things you found.
activities.why: Spotting a shape in real objects shows he understands the shape, not just its picture (CG-8).

activities.title: Soft and rough

hook.say: My feathers are very soft. What else is soft? And what feels rough and scratchy? Let's find out!

activities.fun: Hands-on describing words: soft, rough, smooth, bumpy.
activities.gather_say: You need your fingers.

steps.say: Use your fingers like a scientist. Touch gently.
Find something soft. A pillow? A teddy?
Now find something rough. A coconut shell? A doormat?

stuck.say: Rough feels scratchy. Try the doormat, a coconut shell, or the broom.

steps.say: Tell how each one feels. Soft? Rough? Smooth? Bumpy?

challenge.say: Close your eyes. Amma gives you something to touch. Is it soft or rough?

activities.show: Let Amma or Appa feel your soft and rough things!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me something soft and something rough.
activities.why: Touch words like rough, smooth and bumpy sharpen the senses and add describing words (CG-2, CG-9).

activities.title: Sock pairs

hook.say: The socks had a party and got all mixed up! Can you help each sock find its friend?

activities.fun: A real household job that is a matching puzzle, and Amma gets help.
activities.gather_say: You need clean sock basket.

steps.say: Find two socks that look the same. A pair!

stuck.say: First find socks with the same colour. Then check the pattern.
Hold two socks side by side. Same size? Same stripes? A pair!

steps.say: Now make all the pairs you can.
Count your pairs. Is any sock left without a friend?

challenge.text: Line them up big to small
challenge.say: Line up the pairs: Appa's biggest socks first, your tiny socks last!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa how many pairs you made!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me how many pairs you found.
activities.why: Matching is early logic, and helping with laundry is real seva at home (CG-5, CG-8).

activities.title: Tidy-up treasure hunt

hook.say: Oh no, the toys forgot their way home! Can you find five lost toys and take them home?

activities.fun: Tidying turned into a rescue mission, with counting to five.
activities.gather_say: You need sharp eyes and two hands.

steps.say: Find five toys that are not in their home.
Put each one back where it lives.

stuck.say: Cars live with cars. Books live with books. Where do the others live?

steps.say: Look around. Wow, what a tidy room!

challenge.say: Can you find ten lost things and take them all home? Count as you go!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your tidy room!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me which toys you put back.
activities.why: Tidying is framed as a hunt so that helping feels like play: seva and self-care (CG-1, CG-5).

activities.title: Things that roll

hook.say: I tried to roll a book down a hill. It didn't roll! What things can roll? Let's test!

activities.fun: Guess, test, sort: his first fair test, with a ball and a book.
activities.gather_say: You need a ball, a book, a crayon and a block.

steps.say: Some things roll and some things don't. What do you think will roll?
Find four things: a ball, a book, a crayon, a block.
Push each one gently on the floor. Does it roll?

stuck.say: Give each one gentle push. Did it roll, or just slide?

steps.say: Which ones rolled? What shape are they?

challenge.say: Can you find three more things that roll? A lemon? A round pencil?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa what rolls and what doesn't!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what rolled and what did not.
activities.why: Guess-then-check is the predict and test habit, and it links rolling to round shapes (CG-7, CG-8).

activities.title: Rainbow hunt

hook.say: After the rain, I saw a rainbow over Bangalore! Can you make one with things from home?

activities.fun: Six colours in order: a hunt, then a beautiful line on the floor.
activities.gather_say: You need sharp eyes.

steps.say: Find something red, something orange, and something yellow.
Now find something green, something blue, and something purple.

stuck.say: Purple is tricky! Look at flowers, clothes, or crayons.
Blue might be on clothes, a toy, or a book cover.

steps.say: Line them up on the floor, like a rainbow.
Point to each one and say its colour.

challenge.say: Now make it backwards: purple first, red last!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your rainbow line!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me your rainbow colours.
activities.why: Collecting and ordering colours practises colour names, sequence and memory (CG-2, CG-9).

activities.title: Buh sound hunt

hook.say: My favourite sound is buh! Like ball, book and banana. Can you find buh things for me?

activities.fun: Hearing first sounds in real objects: the root of reading.
activities.gather_say: You need big ears.

steps.say: Listen. Buh, buh, ball. Buh, buh, book. Can you hear the buh sound?
Find things that start with buh. A book? A box? A banana?

stuck.say: Try these: box, bag, bottle, bed, banana. Do they start with buh?

steps.say: Bring two or three buh things.
Say each name slowly. Buh, buh, book!

challenge.say: Can you find five buh things? A bat? A bangle? A brush?

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa your buh words!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me your buh words.
activities.why: Hearing the first sound of a word (phonemic awareness) comes before reading in the UKG phonics path (CG-10).

activities.title: Sss sound hunt

hook.say: A friendly snake taught me his sound: sss! Can you find things that start with sss?

activities.fun: A snake sound hunt: sock, spoon, sofa, sun.
activities.gather_say: You need big ears.

steps.say: Listen. Sss, sock. Sss, spoon. Like a snake: sss!
Find things that start with sss. A sock? A spoon? A slipper?

stuck.say: Try these: sock, spoon, sofa, star, sun. Hear the snake sound?

steps.say: Bring two or three sss things.
Say each name slowly, with a long snake sound.

challenge.say: Line up all your sss things in a long snake line. Sss!

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa your sss words!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me your sss words.
activities.why: Stretching the first sound of a word trains the ear for phonics without any writing (CG-10).

activities.title: Sound hunt

hook.say: I'm starting a band in my nest! I need things that shake, scrunch and clap. Can you find some?

activities.fun: Becoming a sound detective, then a one-boy band.
activities.gather_say: You need big ears and keys.

steps.say: Put on your big listening ears.
Find things that make a sound. Keys? Paper? A book closing?

stuck.say: Shake the keys. Scrunch a paper. Tap a steel plate with a spoon.

steps.say: Make each one make its sound. Shake! Scrunch! Clap!
Which one is loud? Which one is soft?

challenge.say: Play a pattern: shake, shake, clap! Can Amma copy you?

activities.show: Play your sounds for Amma or Appa. Can they guess with closed eyes?
activities.done: Wow! Tell me the loudest sound you found.
activities.why: Comparing loud and soft trains careful listening and describing words (CG-2, CG-12).

activities.title: Heavy or light?

hook.say: I can carry a leaf, but not a book. Which things are heavy and which are light? Let's test!

activities.fun: He is the weighing machine: two hands, two piles.
activities.gather_say: You need two hands.

steps.say: Hold one thing in each hand. A book and a sock.
Which one pulls your hand down more? That one is heavier.

stuck.say: Close your eyes. Which hand feels pulled down? That one is heavy.

steps.say: Try more pairs. A cushion and a ball. A shoe and a spoon.

steps.text: Make a heavy and light pile
steps.say: Make a heavy pile and a light pile.

challenge.say: Line up three things: the lightest, the middle, and the heaviest!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your heavy pile and light pile!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what was heavy and what was light.
activities.why: Comparing weight with his own hands is early measurement, before any scale (CG-8).

activities.title: Shiny things in the kitchen

hook.say: I saw a little bird inside a steel plate! Was it me? Let's find more shiny mirrors!

mission.text: Find your face in shiny things

activities.fun: Steel plates and spoons as mirrors, and the upside-down spoon surprise.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need sharp eyes.

steps.text: Go with Amma to the kitchen
steps.say: Go with Amma to the kitchen. Stay with her.
Find shiny things. A steel plate? A spoon? A katori?
Look into each one. Can you see your face?
Look in the inside of a spoon. Your face is upside down!

stuck.say: Look into the hollow side of the spoon. Hold it a little far from your face.

challenge.say: Now look at the back of the spoon. Is your face still upside down?

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa about the upside-down face!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me where you saw your face.
activities.why: Noticing reflections is real physics he can see for himself, in a safe, supervised kitchen (CG-7).

activities.title: Window watch with Appa

hook.say: My cousins live near your window! Can you sit with Appa and spot my bird friends?

activities.fun: Quiet watching with Appa: crows, pigeons, mynas, and counting scooters.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need sharp eyes.

steps.text: Sit by the window with Appa
steps.say: Sit by the window with Appa. Get comfy.
Look for a bird. A crow? A pigeon? A myna? Just watch quietly.

stuck.say: Birds sit on trees, wires and walls. Look there, very quietly.
Birds fly away from noise. Sit still like a statue.

steps.say: Now count the scooters that go by.
What did you see? Tell Appa one thing.

challenge.say: Can you spot three different birds? A crow, a pigeon and a myna?

activities.show: Tell Amma what you and Appa saw!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you saw from the window.
activities.why: Quiet watching builds attention and nature awareness, safely from inside with a grown-up (CG-6, CG-13).

activities.title: Number hunt

hook.say: The numbers are playing hide and seek! They hide on books, remotes and calendars. Can you find them?

activities.fun: Numbers out in the wild: on the remote, a calendar, page numbers.
activities.gather_say: You need sharp eyes.

steps.say: Numbers hide everywhere! Look where you can reach: the remote, a calendar, a book.
Find one number. What number is it?
Can you find the number of your age? How old are you?

stuck.say: Show your age on your fingers. Now find that number shape!

steps.say: Read the numbers you found to Appa.

challenge.say: Can you find the number one, then two, then three, in order?

activities.show: Show Appa where the numbers were hiding!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me which numbers you found.
activities.why: Finding numerals in the real world builds recognition of 1 to 20 and shows what numbers are for (CG-8).

activities.title: Leaf shapes walk

hook.say: The trees in Lalbagh have so many kinds of leaves! Can you and Appa find three kinds near home?

activities.fun: A nature walk with Appa that trains careful looking: long, many-part, dry.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need sharp eyes.

steps.say: Go out with Appa, to the park or near home. Hold hands.
Look for a long, thin leaf. Just look, and point!

steps.text: Find a leaf with many parts
steps.say: Now find a leaf with many little parts.

stuck.say: A neem tree or a curry leaf plant has many little leaves on one stem.

steps.say: Can you see a brown, dry leaf on the ground?
How many kinds of leaves did you see?

challenge.text: Leaf as big as your hand
challenge.say: Can you find a leaf as big as your hand? Hold your hand near it. Just look!

activities.show: Tell Amma about the leaves you and Appa found!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me about the leaves you saw.
activities.why: Looking closely at leaves builds observation and respect for plants: look, don't pick (CG-6, CG-7).

activities.title: Fast fall, slow fall

hook.say: When I drop a leaf, it floats down slowly. When I drop a pebble, it falls fast! Why? Let's test!

mission.text: Race paper ball and flat paper

activities.fun: Same paper, different shape, different fall: a real air-resistance surprise.
activities.gather_say: You need two same papers.

steps.say: Scrunch one paper into a tight ball. Keep the other flat.
Guess! If you drop them together, which will land first?
Stand on the floor. Hold both up high, and let go together!

stuck.say: Hold both at the same height. Say one, two, three, and open both hands together!

steps.say: Which one was slow? Why do you think so?

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Which paper landed first?

challenge.say: Try a flat paper and a paper folded in four. Which lands first now?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa, and ask them to guess first!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Predict, try, notice, tell: the whole science cycle with two sheets of paper (CG-7).

activities.title: Float or sink

hook.say: My friend the duck says everything floats. I think some things sink! Who is right? Let's test!

activities.fun: Splashy guessing with kitchen things: the coconut shell is the star.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need a big bowl, water, a spoon and a coconut shell.

steps.say: With Amma, put water in a big bowl or a bucket.
Find a spoon, a leaf, a coconut shell, a steel katori, and a crayon.
Hold up the coconut shell. Will it float or sink? Guess for each thing.

steps.text: Put them in one by one
steps.say: Put them in, one by one. Watch carefully.

stuck.say: Put in one thing, then watch. Wait. Then the next one.

steps.say: What floated? What sank? Were your guesses right?

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Did the coconut shell float or sink?

challenge.say: Float a steel katori. How many crayons can it carry before it sinks?

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa which surprised you!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Float and sink is the classic first experiment: he learns to guess, test and change his mind (CG-7).

activities.title: Hand shadows

hook.say: A big dark bird is on the wall! Is it me? Let's make shadow animals with a torch!

activities.fun: Shadow puppets in a dark room: magic that is really light science.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need a torch and a wall.

steps.say: Ask Appa for a torch, and close the curtains together.
Appa shines the torch on the wall. Put your hand in the light.
Hook your thumbs together and flap. A bird!

stuck.say: Cross your hands, hook your thumbs, spread your fingers wide, and flap!
Ask Appa to make the bird first. Then copy his hands.

steps.say: Guess: will the shadow grow or shrink? Now move your hand near the torch.
What made the shadow bigger? Tell Appa.

activities.guess_back: Were you right? What did the shadow do?

challenge.say: Make a rabbit: two fingers up for ears. Can it hop?

activities.show: Do a shadow show for Amma!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Shadows show that light travels in straight lines and gets blocked: real physics in play (CG-7).

activities.title: Ice melting race

hook.say: Two ice cubes want a race! One sits in the sun, one in the shade. Which melts first?

activities.fun: Peeking again and again at sun versus shade: patience plus a clear result.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need two ice cubes and two plates.

steps.say: Ask Amma for two ice cubes from the fridge, on two plates.

steps.text: One in sun, one in shade
steps.say: Put one plate in the sun and one plate in the shade.
Guess! Which ice will melt first?
Go and play a little. Then peek at the ice again. And again!

stuck.say: Play something, then peek again. Ice melts slowly. Peek, play, peek!

steps.say: Which one became water first? Why?

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Which ice melted first?

challenge.say: Try again, but wrap one ice cube in a hanky. Does it melt slower or faster?

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa which ice melted first!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Watching ice turn to water shows heat changing a material, a UKG melt-and-freeze idea (CG-7).

activities.title: Colour magic water

hook.say: I want to paint my nest a new colour! Amma has magic yellow and pink in the kitchen. Let's mix!

activities.fun: Turmeric and beetroot become paint: colour mixing with real food colours.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need two katoris, water, a spoon and paper.

steps.say: Ask Amma to mix a pinch of turmeric into a katori of water. Yellow!
Amma makes pink water with a piece of beetroot. Pink!
Guess! If we mix yellow and pink, what colour will we get?
Put one spoon of each into a new katori. Stir!
Dip your finger and paint on paper. What colour is it?

stuck.say: Dip just one fingertip. Then draw slowly on the paper.

activities.guess_back: Were you right? What colour did you make?

challenge.say: Add more water to your colour. Does it get lighter or darker?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your colour painting!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Mixing kitchen colours shows that two colours make a new one, with nothing bought (CG-7, CG-12).

activities.title: Sprouting seeds

hook.say: I found some tiny green moong seeds. Are they asleep? Can we wake them up with water?

activities.fun: A slow story over a few days: watching for the tiny white root.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need a katori, cotton, moong seeds and water.

steps.say: With Amma, put some wet cotton in a katori.
Amma gives you a few green moong seeds. Place them on the cotton.
What do you think the seeds will do?
Each morning, sprinkle a little water with Amma.

stuck.say: Water them every morning, after you brush your teeth.
Only a few drops. With too much water, the seeds can't breathe.

steps.say: Look every day. Do you see a tiny white tail? That's a root!

activities.guess_back: Were you right? What are your seeds doing?

challenge.say: Put a second katori in a dark cupboard. Do those seeds grow differently?

later.say: How are your seeds? Show me!

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your seeds every morning!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Seeds sprouting over days teaches what plants need and builds patient observation (CG-6, CG-7).

activities.title: Ramp race

hook.say: Ready, steady, go! The ball and the car want to race down a hill. Which goes further?

activities.fun: A fair race: same start, no pushing, then make the hill steeper.
activities.gather_say: You need books, a ball and a toy car.

steps.say: Put one end of a big book on a pile of small books. A slope!
Choose two racers. A cricket ball and a toy car?
Guess! Which one will go further?
Hold them at the top. Ready, steady, let go!

stuck.say: Just open your hands and let go. No pushing! Then it's fair.

steps.say: Add one more book. Make it steeper. What changes?

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Which racer went further?

challenge.say: Put a sock where each racer stops. Which one went further?

activities.show: Race your racers for Amma or Appa!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Changing one thing (the slope) and seeing what happens is the heart of a fair test (CG-7, CG-8).

activities.title: Comb magic

hook.say: Can a comb do magic? I heard it can make paper jump! Let's find out!

activities.fun: Static electricity that looks like magic, using only a comb and paper.
activities.gather_say: You need paper and a plastic comb.

steps.say: Tear some tiny bits of paper. Put them on the table.

steps.text: Rub a comb in your hair
steps.say: Rub a plastic comb in your dry hair. Fast, ten times!

stuck.say: Your hair must be dry. Rub fast, ten times, one way.
Tear the bits tiny, smaller than your fingernail.

steps.say: Guess! What will the comb do to the paper?
Hold the comb just above the paper bits. Whoa! They jump up!

activities.guess_back: Were you right? What did the paper do?

challenge.say: Try a tiny piece of tissue paper. Does it jump higher?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa your comb magic!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Static is invisible but its effect is clear, so he learns that not everything that works can be seen (CG-7).

activities.title: Tumbler music

hook.say: I love to sing! Can steel tumblers sing too? Let's make tumbler music!

activities.fun: Ting, ting, tong: hearing high and low notes he made with water.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need three steel tumblers, water and a spoon.

steps.say: With Amma, pour a little water in one, more in the next, lots in the last.
Guess which will sound high. Now tap each tumbler gently with a spoon. Ting!

stuck.say: Tap the side of the tumbler gently, near the top. Ting!

steps.say: Which one sounds high? Which one sounds low?
Play a little tune. Ting, ting, tong!

guess_choices.say: The one with a little water.
The one with lots of water.

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Which tumbler sang the highest?

challenge.say: Can you play the start of Twinkle Twinkle? Low, low, high, high!

activities.show: Play your tumbler tune for everyone!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Hearing how water changes a note links sound, music and comparing amounts (CG-7, CG-12).

activities.title: Soak it up

hook.say: Oops! I spilled water in my nest. Which thing will drink it up best? Let's test!

activities.fun: Cloth, paper or plastic: finding out what soaks, the reason towels work.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need a little water, a plate, a cloth, newspaper and a plastic cup.

steps.text: A little water on a plate
steps.say: With Amma, put a spoon of water on a plate.
Guess! Which will soak up the water: cloth, newspaper, or a plastic cup?
Try each one on the water. Press gently. Use the bottom of the cup.

stuck.say: Press it on the water. Count one, two, three. Then lift it up and look.

steps.say: Which one drank the water? Which one did not?

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Which one drank the water?

challenge.say: Test a tissue and a leaf too. Which one is the best drinker now?

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa the best water-drinker!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Testing materials shows that things are chosen for a job: why towels are cloth, not plastic (CG-7).

activities.title: Water up, water over

hook.say: I dropped a pebble into my water bowl, and the water spilled out! Will a spoon do that too?

activities.fun: Watching water climb as spoons go in: the start of volume.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need a steel tumbler, a plate, water and spoons.

steps.say: Put a steel tumbler on a plate.
With Amma, fill the tumbler with water, right to the top.
Guess! If we drop a spoon in, what will the water do?
Drop in one spoon, slowly. Then another. Watch the top!

stuck.say: Hold the spoon at the top and let it slide in slowly. Watch the top of the water!

steps.say: Look at the plate. Where did the water come from?

guess_choices.say: The water goes up and spills.

activities.guess_back: Were you right? What did the water do?

challenge.say: Fill it again. How many spoons can go in before the water spills?

activities.show: Show Amma or Appa the water on the plate!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Seeing objects push water up and over is a first feel for volume, the idea behind Archimedes' bath (CG-7, CG-8).

activities.title: Paper boat

hook.say: Thatha told me about paper boats in the rain! Can you and Appa make one and make it sail?

mission.text: Make a paper boat with Appa

activities.fun: The classic monsoon craft, folded with Appa, then a real sail across the bowl.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need newspaper, a big bowl and water.

steps.say: Appa looks at the folding pictures. Fold together, step by step. Press each fold flat.

stuck.say: Ask Appa to open the folding pictures. Fold one step, press it flat, then the next.

steps.say: Open it up. It's a boat! Guess: will it float?
With Appa, put water in a bucket or a big bowl. Float your boat!
Blow gently behind the boat. It sails! What happens when the paper gets wet?

stuck.say: Bend down low and blow softly behind the boat. Not too hard!

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Did your boat float?

challenge.say: Can your boat carry one crayon? Or two?

grownup_steps.text: Start with a rectangle: half a newspaper sheet (Appa tears or cuts it).
Fold it in half, top edge down to the bottom edge. Fold at the top.
Fold both top corners down to meet in the middle. It looks like a house.
Fold the bottom strip up on the front. Turn over, fold the back strip up. A hat!
Open the hat from the bottom, bring the two ends together, press flat: a diamond.
Fold the bottom point up to the top, front and back. A triangle.
Open it from the bottom again and press flat into a smaller diamond.
Gently pull the two top points apart. The boat pops open. Shape it with your fingers.

activities.show: Show Amma your boat sailing!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Folding along steps builds sequencing, and a soggy boat starts a talk about why paper soaks water (CG-7, CG-12).

activities.title: Which hanky dries first?

hook.say: Amma hangs clothes out to dry, all spread out. Why not scrunched up? Let's find out!

activities.fun: Explains why we spread clothes to dry; the result comes after lunch.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need two hankies and water.

steps.say: With Amma, wet two hankies and squeeze them out.
Spread one hanky out flat. Scrunch the other into a ball.

stuck.say: Spread one flat like a chapati. Squeeze the other into a tight ball.

steps.say: Guess! Which one will dry first?
After lunch, touch both. Which one is dry?
Why did that one dry first? Tell Amma your idea.

activities.guess_back: Were you right? Which hanky dried first?

challenge.say: Wet two hankies again. Put one under the fan. Which dries first now?

later.say: Did you touch the two hankies? Which one is dry?

activities.show: Tell Amma or Appa why we spread clothes to dry!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: Links an experiment to a daily chore: spreading out helps water go into the air (CG-5, CG-7).

activities.title: Day and night

hook.say: Every evening the sun goes away. Where does it go? Let's find out with a torch!

activities.fun: A torch sun and a ball Earth: he turns the world himself.
activities.gather_say: Ask Amma or Appa to help. You need a torch, a ball and a crayon.

steps.say: Appa holds the torch. The torch is the Sun!
A ball is our Earth. Hold it up in the light.
Draw a small dot on the ball. That's our home, Bangalore!
Guess: what happens to our home as it turns? Turn the ball slowly.

stuck.say: Turn the ball very slowly. Keep your eyes on the dot.

steps.say: When the dot faces the torch, it's day. Turned away, it's night!

activities.guess_back: Were you right? What happened to our home?

challenge.say: Draw a dot for Ajji's town too. Is it day there when it's day here?

activities.show: Show Amma how day and night happen!
activities.done: Wow! Tell me what you discovered.
activities.why: A torch and a ball make day and night something he can act out and explain (CG-7).
